fields.meta_title: Invoice Automation Software, Built From a Prompt | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Describe the invoices you get and the ones you send. Emergent builds invoice automation that reads vendor PDFs and bills your clients.
fields.h1: Build Invoice Automation That Reads Bills and Sends Invoices
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent which invoices you receive and which you send. It builds the app that turns vendor PDFs into ledger entries and bills customers from hours or finished jobs.
fields.features_heading: What Invoice Automation Has to Handle
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds invoice automation for the bills that arrive in your inbox and the invoices your team sends out each month.
fields.feature_1:
Field extraction with a review queue

Reads vendor, invoice number, dates, PO number and each line item from PDFs and scans. A field the model is unsure of goes to a review queue, not straight to the ledger.
fields.feature_2:
Duplicate checks before anything posts

Compares every new invoice with that vendor's history on number, amount and date. A resent PDF under a new filename is held, and the first copy stays the bill of record.
fields.feature_3:
GL coding line by line

Gives each line a GL account and cost center based on how that vendor's lines were coded before. Anything new waits for a person, and their choice is applied the next time.
fields.feature_4:
Invoices generated from your records

Creates outgoing invoices from timesheets or closed jobs, using your own numbering and payment terms. Each invoice is saved as a PDF and a database row before anyone sends it.
fields.feature_5:
Sent with a payment link, then posted

Emails each invoice with a Stripe payment link or one from the processor you connect, then posts it to QuickBooks or Xero. The dashboard lists every invoice still unpaid.
fields.feature_6:
Every rule exported to your GitHub

The extraction and coding logic is exported to your GitHub repository, where an engineer can trace why any field was held. Invoice records live in a database you own.

fields.tab_content_1:
One bill record per PDF, with unsure fields held

Vendor invoices emailed to the AP inbox are read into vendor, invoice number, dates, line items and total. Globex Industrial's INV-20817 comes through at $3,412.50, but the due date sits under a smudge on the scan. That one field waits for Maria Lopez to confirm, and every other field is already filled.
fields.tab_content_2:
Code each line from the vendor's own history

Each line on a supplier invoice takes the GL account that the same item from that vendor got last time. On Initech Supply's six-line invoice, five lines are coded on arrival. The label printer, $240.00 and never bought from them before, goes to Sam Ortiz in finance to pick an account.
fields.tab_content_3:
Billable hours become client invoices on the 1st

Hours logged against each client in October turn into one draft invoice per client on Nov 1. Acme's draft comes to $6,300.00, for 42 hours at $150. Ana Ruiz reviews the four drafts in one list, and nothing goes out until she approves. Each invoice then leaves by email with a Stripe payment link.
fields.tab_content_4:
The customer has the invoice before the van leaves

A technician closes the job on a phone, and the labor and parts on it become an invoice. Job 4471 bills 1.5 hours at $120 and a $68.40 shutoff valve, $248.40 in all. Dana Whitfield gets it by email with a payment link, and the PDF stays attached to the job record.

fields.howto_description: Start with a stack of real invoices, not a blank template. The first steps decide what the app reads and what it sends; the later ones connect it and put it in front of your team.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Collect a month of real invoices
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Connect the inbox and your sources
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull twenty invoices you received last month and five you sent. Include the hard ones: a phone photo, a scan with a stamp across the total, a two-page PDF. These samples show Emergent what the app has to read and what your own invoices look like.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe what lands in each bill record: vendor, invoice number, invoice and due dates, PO number, every line and the total. Name the fields a person must confirm before anything posts, for example any total over $10,000 or a vendor seen for the first time.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect the inbox vendors already email; nobody outside has to change a habit. For invoices you send, connect wherever billable work is recorded: a timesheet tool, a field service app, or Stripe orders. Emergent builds a sync for each one through its API.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which field settles the GL account: the vendor, the item description or the department. Then tell Emergent what counts as a duplicate in your books, such as the same vendor and amount within 30 days, and who reviews a held invoice.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give Emergent your current invoice PDF and list the changes you want: a numbering format, payment terms, your logo, the payment link. Every invoice the app sends follows that template, and each one is stored as a PDF beside its database row.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Post to the ledger in parallel
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect QuickBooks or Xero. Bills you receive post with their GL codes and the source PDF attached; invoices you send post as receivables. Run last month's invoices through the app first and compare its entries with the ones your team made by hand.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Go live and watch the review queue
fields.howto_step_7_des: Switch the inbox over at the start of a month. On the dashboard, track how many fields reach the review queue each week. When one vendor's invoices keep needing the same fix, ask Emergent for a rule that handles that vendor's layout.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Invoice Automation That Reads Bills and Sends Invoices' and hero ('turns vendor PDFs into ledger entries and bills customers from hours or finished jobs') state both directions, per the watch-list split from the AP page.

intent.evidence: Explainer-and-vendor SERP: definition first (FAQ 1), how processing works, AI vs OCR, the QuickBooks and free-app PAA questions answered with sourced facts, and a how-to specific to invoices.

specificity.evidence: Finance vocabulary: 'GL account and cost center', 'bill of record', 'INV-20817', 'post as receivables', 'a scan with a stamp across the total'; the AP variant is used as QC Q4 requires for this competitor set.

openers.evidence: Five feature bodies open on subjectless fragments (CONTENT_DEFECTS #2, #16): 'Reads vendor, invoice number...', 'Compares every new invoice...', 'Gives each line a GL account...', 'Creates outgoing invoices...', 'Emails each invoice...'.

craft.evidence: Ideas restated across fields (CONTENT_DEFECTS #21): PDF plus database row (feature_4, howto_step_5), posting to QuickBooks or Xero (feature_5, howto_step_6), GL coding from vendor history (feature_3, tab_content_2), sources of outgoing invoices (feature_4, FAQ 2, howto_step_3, FAQ 9).

voice.evidence: Concrete and unglamorous: 'the due date sits under a smudge on the scan', 'The label printer, $240.00 and never bought from them before'. No AI tells.

truth.evidence: Third-party facts match their sources (QuickBooks recurring invoices and free generator, Zoho Invoice free plan, BILL AP and AR, Stampli's Billy, Stripe hosted invoice page); Emergent claims map to prompt-build, ai-extraction, api-connect, code-export, database-owned, free-start; every drawn total adds up.

distinct.evidence: why_description, feature_6, howto_step_6 and howto_step_7 repeat the sibling accounts-payable-automation page with the nouns swapped (CONTENT_DEFECTS #22): 'Invoice tools keep your coding rules inside their app. Emergent writes them as code in your GitHub repo, changed by prompting.' versus AP 'In an AP suite, your approval rules live inside the vendor's app. With Emergent they are code in your repo, changed by prompting.'

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic items, 5 PAA, 4 secondaries, 1 definition; each answers in its first sentence ('Yes, for recurring invoices.'); links to AP, AR and approval-workflow carry the scope split.

images.evidence: All numbers add up and match the copy: $3,412.50 with the due date held for Maria Lopez; 5 of 6 lines coded with the $240.00 label printer to Sam Ortiz; Acme 42 h x $150 = $6,300 within $13,860 across four drafts for Ana Ruiz; 1.5 h x $120 + $68.40 = $248.40 to Dana Whitfield at a reserved domain.

findings.quote: Invoice tools keep your coding rules inside their app. Emergent writes them as code in your GitHub repo, changed by prompting.
findings.issue: The sibling /ai-automation-builder/accounts-payable-automation with the nouns swapped. Every instance: why_description versus AP 'In an AP suite, your approval rules live inside the vendor's app. With Emergent they are code in your repo, changed by prompting.'; feature_6 'The extraction and coding logic is exported to your GitHub repository, where an engineer can trace why any field was held. Invoice records live in a database you own.' versus AP feature_6 'The matching rules and approval chain export to your GitHub repository, where an engineer can read exactly why a bill was held. Bill and payment records stay in a database you own.'; howto_step_6 '06 Post to the ledger in parallel ... Run last month's invoices through the app first and compare its entries with the ones your team made by hand.' versus AP '06 Test with last month's invoices ... Run last month's invoices through the automated AP workflow before go-live ... differs from what your team did by hand'; howto_step_7 '07 Go live and watch the review queue / Switch the inbox over at the start of a month. On the dashboard, track ... When one vendor's invoices keep needing the same fix, ask Emergent for a rule' versus AP '07 Go live and watch cycle time / Point the AP inbox at the workflow on the first day of a payment cycle. On the dashboard, watch ... If approvers keep releasing held bills unchanged, ask Emergent to widen'.
findings.fix: Rewrite each field from this page's own angle (both directions of an invoice). why_description could contrast the two-tool setup ('Most teams read bills in one tool and send invoices from another'); feature_6 could name what an engineer extends (a new vendor layout, a client's invoice format); steps 6 and 7 need their own shapes, for example a parallel month comparing sent-invoice totals with the timesheet tool, and a go-live that starts with outgoing invoices.

The row #16 fix names a subject; approved pages open with a subject or an imperative.
findings.fix: Give each a subject or an imperative, varied: 'Each PDF or scan is read into vendor, invoice number...'; 'A resent PDF under a new filename is held...'; 'Outgoing invoices are built from timesheets or closed jobs...'.
